checks_performed: Read only the authorized source and draft JSON files; used no web sources.
Reconstructed the planar-duality, colouring, perimeter, forest-partition, quadrilateral-switch, and skeleton arguments independently.
Checked the supplied source proof that simple 2-vertex-connected series-parallel graphs have CAI-partitions and verified its hypotheses for bichromatic dual graphs.
Ran an exact Boolean enumeration of all 512 labelled bipartite graphs on 3+3 vertices; exactly K3,3 and its nine one-edge deletions have feedback-vertex number at least two.
Ran an exact-integer enumeration of all counterexample-compatible face profiles for n=2m through m=15; counts are zero for m=2 through 12, one for m=13, zero for m=14, and nine for m=15.

claims.claim: The planar dual T of G is a simple Eulerian plane triangulation with a proper vertex 3-colouring I1,I2,I3, unique up to permuting the colours.
claims.evidence: Three-connectivity makes facial boundaries simple and excludes primal edge cuts of size one or two, so the dual has neither loops nor parallel edges. Cubicity makes every dual face triangular, while bipartiteness makes every primal face even and hence every dual degree even. Starting with three colours on one triangle, propagation across adjacent triangles is forced. Its only local consistency obstruction is traversal around a dual vertex, and even degree makes that traversal consistent; on the sphere these local walks generate all consistency checks. Propagation also proves uniqueness up to the initial permutation.
claims.search_method: Direct planar-duality and colour-propagation proof from the target assumptions.

claims.claim: For each colour i, the boundaries of the primal faces corresponding to Ii are pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles covering V(G). Moreover, each colour class has total face perimeter n=|V(G)|, G has n/2+2 faces, and it has at least six quadrilateral faces.
claims.evidence: The three faces incident with each primal vertex form a dual triangle and therefore have distinct colours. Exactly one face of each colour contains each primal vertex, proving disjointness, coverage, and perimeter n. Cubicity gives |E|=3n/2 and Euler gives |F|=n/2+2. Thus sum_f(6-|f|)=12. Every facial cycle has even length at least four, so quadrilaterals contribute 2, hexagons 0, and longer faces negatively; consequently there are at least six quadrilaterals.
claims.search_method: Exact incidence counting and Euler-formula derivation.

claims.claim: G is Hamiltonian if and only if V(T) can be partitioned into two sets inducing forests.
claims.evidence: Let N=|V(T)|. For a partition into induced forests X,Y, every triangular face has exactly two cross-edges, giving 2N-4 cross-edges and N-2 internal edges. The forests have N-cX-cY internal edges, so cX=cY=1 and both are trees. The dual primal edges form a spanning 2-factor; if it had k cycles, their complement on the sphere would have k+1 regions, whereas the two induced dual trees give exactly two regions, forcing k=1. Conversely, a Hamiltonian cycle separates primal faces into two disks. Face adjacency within each disk is connected, and the N-2 noncycle dual edges meet the exact lower bound for two connected induced subgraphs, so both are trees.
claims.search_method: Direct edge counting and Jordan-curve duality proof in both directions.

claims.claim: If any bichromatic graph H=T[Ii union Ij] has a CAI-partition, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: Write the CAI-partition as A union J, where T[A] is a tree and J is independent. If T[J union Ik] contained a cycle, connectedness of A places A wholly on one side. In the fan at a cycle vertex toward the other side, two consecutive neighbours together with that vertex form a triangle contained in J union Ik, impossible because J and Ik are each independent. Hence J union Ik induces a forest, and Claim 2 yields a Hamiltonian cycle.
claims.search_method: Independent reconstruction of the supplied planar triangle argument followed by Claim 2.

claims.claim: In particular, G is Hamiltonian whenever some bichromatic graph T[Ii union Ij] is series-parallel.
claims.evidence: Deleting one colour class from a simple Eulerian triangulation produces a simple 2-vertex-connected bichromatic graph. The supplied source proves that every simple 2-vertex-connected series-parallel graph has a CAI-partition via a short nested ear decomposition. Claim 3 then applies.
claims.search_method: Checked the source theorem proof and matched all of its hypotheses to the bichromatic graph.

claims.claim: For distinct colours i,j, let Qij have the i-coloured faces as vertices, with one edge for every j-coloured quadrilateral joining the two i-coloured faces opposite it. Then G has a spanning 2-factor with exactly c(Qij) cycles. In particular, connected Qij certifies Hamiltonicity.
claims.evidence: Begin with the facial 2-factor from colour i. At a j-coloured quadrilateral, its boundary alternates between factor and nonfactor edges, and its two incident i-faces are distinct. Choose a spanning forest of Qij and toggle the four boundary edges for its quadrilaterals. Same-colour quadrilaterals are vertex-disjoint. Inductively, an unprocessed forest edge joins two distinct current components, so its toggle merges exactly two cycles. Starting from |V(Qij)| cycles and performing |V(Qij)|-c(Qij) merges leaves exactly c(Qij) cycles.
claims.search_method: Direct induction over a spanning forest of the auxiliary multigraph.

claims.claim: Every target graph on n vertices has a spanning 2-factor with at most floor((n+4)/6)-1 cycles.
claims.evidence: Let a be the smallest face-colour-class size. Since there are n/2+2 faces, a is at most floor((n+4)/6). If a=1, its single facial boundary is Hamiltonian; the required bound is at least one because a target graph has n>=8. Otherwise, at least one of the other two colours contains a quadrilateral: if neither did, both class sizes and therefore also a would be at most n/6, contradicting the total n/2+2. That quadrilateral supplies a nonloop edge in Qij, so c(Qij)<=a-1. Claim 5 gives the asserted bound.
claims.search_method: Exact symbolic face-count argument, including the a=1 and a>=2 cases.

claims.claim: Let H be 2-vertex-connected. Suppress its maximal degree-2 paths to a multigraph K, let B be the vertices of degree at least three, and let U=H[B], the unsubdivided skeleton edges. If U is a forest, or U-v is a forest for some v in B, then H has a CAI-partition.
claims.evidence: If B is empty, H is a cycle and deleting one vertex gives the partition. Otherwise set W empty in the first case and W={v} in the second. Two-connectivity makes K-W connected and excludes a skeleton loop at v. Extend U-W to a spanning tree R of K-W. Every non-tree skeleton edge not incident with W is subdivided; choose one internal vertex from each corresponding path and add W to the independent set. These choices are mutually nonadjacent. Their complement consists of the subdivided tree R plus path fragments attached at only one endpoint, including paths formerly incident with v, and is therefore an induced connected tree.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof covering the cycle, forest, and one-vertex-deletion cases.

claims.claim: In any counterexample, every face-colour class contains at least three nonquadrilateral faces; for every colour pair, their nonquadrilateral-face adjacency graph has feedback-vertex number at least two. Moreover, every Qij is disconnected and every bichromatic graph is non-series-parallel.
claims.evidence: In a bichromatic graph, degree is half the corresponding primal face length, so the skeleton vertices are exactly the nonquadrilateral faces and U is their adjacency graph. A counterexample admits no bichromatic CAI-partition; by Claim 7, every U has feedback-vertex number at least two. If either bipartition side of U had at most two vertices, deleting at most one of them would destroy every bipartite cycle, a contradiction. Finally, connected Qij and series-parallel bichromatic graphs are excluded respectively by Claims 5 and 4.
claims.search_method: Contraposition of Claims 3–7 with a complete bipartite-cycle case analysis.

claims.claim: If two face-colour classes each consist of exactly three hexagons together with any number of quadrilaterals, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: The associated skeleton U is a simple bipartite graph on 3+3 hexagon vertices. Absence of a CAI-partition would require U-v to contain a cycle for every vertex v. Exact enumeration of all 512 adjacency matrices found precisely ten possibilities: K3,3 and its nine one-edge deletions. K3,3 is nonplanar. For K3,3 minus one edge, four degree-three vertices are saturated and the two missing-edge endpoints have exactly one unused incidence each, so every degree-two vertex lies on a path joining those endpoints. This makes H a subdivision of K3,3, again contradicting planarity.
claims.search_method: Exact exhaustive Boolean enumeration followed by a direct degree and planarity argument.

claims.claim: Every graph satisfying the target assumptions with at most 30 vertices is Hamiltonian; consequently these arguments force every counterexample to have at least 32 vertices.
claims.evidence: For n=2m the exact identities are 2qi+3ri+si=m in each colour and r+s=m-4 globally. Claim 8 gives ri>=3. The checker exhaustively enumerated all nonnegative integer profiles satisfying these identities: none exist for m<=12 or m=14; the unique m=13 profile and all nine m=15 profiles contain at least two classes with (ri,si)=(3,0). Those classes contain exactly three hexagons and otherwise quadrilaterals, so Claim 9 proves Hamiltonicity. Thus no counterexample has n<=30. Cubicity forces n even, making 32 the next possible order.
claims.search_method: Exact exhaustive integer enumeration plus application of Claim 9.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof that every finite simple cubic 3-vertex-connected bipartite planar graph is Hamiltonian or one explicit qualifying non-Hamiltonian graph. The draft explicitly disclaims both and establishes only sufficient criteria, structural restrictions, and the case n<=30. All listed subsidiary claims survive audit, so this is material but incomplete progress: target_verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. The draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is therefore ACCURATE, and its final writeup does not overstate target coverage.
